statements.status_notes: PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120143 (PostgreSQL transition-table cursor use-after-free executes arbitrary code) in 16.16 on the PostgreSQL 16 branch: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120143/ lists 16.16 as the fixed release for major version 16, and the 16.16 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/16.16/, list this CVE. The fix is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/5b2bd1dc1232937762b75c73ee5aea275857a58a on the REL_16_STABLE branch, which changes src/backend/executor/spi.c, src/backend/utils/mmgr/portalmem.c and src/include/utils/portal.h (plus documentation) so that portals over trigger transition tables are closed when the SPI connection ends; it is tagged Security: CVE-2026-120143 and Backpatch-through: 14; that commit is in the REL_16_16 release tag and not in REL_16_15. The DHI postgresql16 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD, https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/859fa0795e895af033fab32094a83301f2b4d8ff/community/postgresql16/APKBUILD, which builds the upstream PostgreSQL release tarball; none of the patches it applies touch the files this fix changes. We checked the postgres server binary, /usr/libexec/postgresql16/postgres, in every published postgresql16 package for Alpine 3.23 on both x86_64 and aarch64 (checksums verified against the package index): 16.16-r0 reports PostgreSQL 16.16 and carries the fix, while the earlier builds 16.13-r0, 16.14-r0 and 16.15-r0 report 16.13, 16.14 and 16.15 and are affected. 16.16-r0 is the first published build that carries the fix. Alpine's postgresql16 APKBUILD lists CVE-2026-120143 under its 16.16-r0 secfixes.

CVE-2026-120143 (PostgreSQL transition-table cursor use-after-free executes arbitrary code) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 17.12: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120143/ and the 17.12 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/. 17.12 is the fixed release listed for major version 17. Alpine's postgresql17 17.12-r0 on the 3.23-stable branch is the upgrade to upstream 17.12 and lists CVE-2026-120143 under its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql17 17.12-r0 package for Alpine 3.23 is built from that APKBUILD and the upstream 17.12 source release, and its postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on both x86_64 and aarch64. Every earlier published build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0 and 17.11-r0) is an earlier upstream release whose server binary reports that older version, so it is affected; 17.12-r0 and later carry the fix.

CVE-2026-120143 (PostgreSQL transition-table cursor use-after-free executes arbitrary code) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 18.7 for major version 18. The PostgreSQL security page, https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120143/, lists 18.7 as the fixed release for 18, the 18.7 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/18.7/, list this CVE, and the CVE record, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120143, lists 18 as affected before 18.7. The fix on the REL_18_STABLE branch is commit https://github.com/postgres/postgres/commit/983bcb768a9ae0fe16ef491b53176bf3e2d06866, which carries the trailer "Security: CVE-2026-120143", is contained in the REL_18_7 tag and not in REL_18_6, and makes SPI_finish() in src/backend/executor/spi.c drop any portal (cursor) that still depends on the SPI connection's query environment, through a new DropQueryEnvPortals() function in src/backend/utils/mmgr/portalmem.c, so that a cursor over a trigger's transition table can no longer outlive the trigger function; its other changes are the declaration in src/include/utils/portal.h and a documentation note in doc/src/sgml/spi.sgml. Alpine's postgresql18 18.7-r0 on the 3.23-stable branch upgrades to the upstream 18.7 release and lists CVE-2026-120143 under 18.7-r0 in its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/59a1f1d230675807d5a95a0c1e57ba5d640ba039/main/postgresql18/APKBUILD. None of the Alpine patches applied in that APKBUILD change the files the fix touches. The DHI postgresql18 18.7-r0 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from that APKBUILD and the upstream PostgreSQL 18.7 source tarball. The DHI Alpine 3.23 package repository (main and security, x86_64 and aarch64) publishes packages built from source postgresql18 at 18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0, 18.6-r0 and 18.7-r0. The vulnerable code is in the postgres server binary, usr/libexec/postgresql18/postgres, in the postgresql18 package. In the 18.7-r0 build the postgres server binary reports PostgreSQL 18.7 on both x86_64 and aarch64, and in each earlier build (18.1-r0, 18.2-r0, 18.3-r0, 18.4-r0 and 18.6-r0) it reports that older 18.x release on both architectures. The earlier builds are upstream releases before 18.7, so they are affected; 18.7-r0 and later carry the fix.

PostgreSQL fixed CVE-2026-120143, a use after free through a cursor over a trigger transition table that lets an object creator execute arbitrary code, in 17.12 (https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-120143/, https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120143, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.12/). Earlier 17 releases are affected. The server binary in this owner's 17.12-0 build and in its rebuild of Debian's 17.12-0+deb13u1 reports PostgreSQL 17.12 on amd64 and arm64, so both carry the fix. The 17.11-1 build and the current rebuild of Debian's 17.11-0+deb13u1 report PostgreSQL 17.11, and the earlier rebuilds of Debian's 17.10-0+deb13u1 and 17.11-0+deb13u1, no longer in the repository, package PostgreSQL 17.10 and 17.11. All of these are affected and sort below 17.12-0.
